account:
Today I inspected the mill's grain stock, visited the office, and took tea with my neighbour. There were eighty hay bales at the mill stall this morning, priced at two emeralds apiece. I heard that the innkeeper needed grain and that builder and freight were involved in finding payment for nineteen bales, possibly through authorized spare planks or services. I personally saw builder hand planks to baker at 11:26, but did not see a grain purchase. My neighbour says baker filled a large bread order, and a towns person reported seeing innkeeper carrying bread. Those are not proof that the grain arrangements were settled.

An odd, persistent rumour describes a bridge or port change at the bakery. Reports place baker, innkeeper and freight there, but nobody I have asked has supplied a concrete proposal. Baker, through my neighbour, and freight directly have denied knowing of any verified change. It may concern private bread supply and transport arrangements rather than public policy; I cannot establish that yet.

The missing town account figures remain unexplained. Secretary previously searched the great hall table chests and found no records, only bread in one chest. No council correspondence or account figures have reached secretary today. I do not know who holds the figures, and have no evidence connecting their absence to the bread dealings.

This evening's gathering deserves attention. My approved appointment is an eighteen hundred great hall lighting inspection with builder, following installation of eight lanterns. Freight requested an operations discussion at that same hour and offered to escort me into the hall. Secretary has repeatedly preserved the lighting inspection first, followed by operations. Freight has now arrived, but secretary has no fresh confirmation from builder. I am at the entrance just before eighteen hundred, ready to go in. The apparent purpose is inspection and routine ferry/warehouse business; the overlapping arrangements and vague rumours make me curious, but I have not witnessed evidence of a concealed plan.
